name: Crypto Scam - Fund Diversion
teaches: The headline case: 5 ETH leaves one wallet, splits across two branches, pays gas at every hop, and reconciles exactly. Also shows one link we can only infer.

name: Simple Scam
teaches: The baseline: victim to scam wallet to exchange, one hop each, nothing hidden.

name: Multi-Hop Forward Tracing
teaches: How far forward a trace can carry a single quantity with no splitting and no loss.

name: Cross-Chain via Bridge
teaches: Where a trace honestly stops: funds leave the source chain, and the destination leg is a different asset we will not pretend to convert.

name: Clean pass-through
teaches: What a fully reconciled trace looks like: one wallet, one transfer per hop, no splitting and no loss.

name: Split with an unattributable remainder
teaches: Why reconciliation matters: most of the quantity is placed, but a real remainder cannot be and is reported instead of spread thin.

name: Co-mingled wallet (poison-pill)
teaches: What Poison actually claims: it cannot tell which outputs are clean, so it over-attributes on purpose. Compare it against pro-rata.

name: Change, fees and contract calls
teaches: Why a naive wallet-to-wallet graph overstates movement: change, fees and contract interactions are not transfers and are excluded here.

name: Derived pairing vs confirmed transfer
teaches: What 'derived' means: a UTXO input/output pairing is computed by our normaliser, not recorded by the chain as a transfer between those addresses.
